overview: France is a great country for students who want to **Study postgraduate in mechanical engineering****. French universities and engineering schools have master’s programs with a focus on fields such as advanced manufacturing, robotics, automotive engineering, aerospace technology, materials science, energy systems and product design.

Students enrolled in a ****Master’s in Mechanical Engineering in France**** gain technical knowledge through theory, lab work, research projects and industry experience. Specializations can be undertaken by international students leading to careers in engineering design, manufacturing, research and development, automation and mechanical systems.
Students can avail these opportunities through ****Edu Hawk worldwide** study abroad guidance** and get to know the requirements involved in pursuing education overseas.

sections.title: 1. Can I do a PG in Mechanical Engineering in France after BTech or BE?

items: Yes. Students pursuing **BTech or BE in Mechanical Engineering** are eligible to apply for postgraduate courses in mechanical engineering, automotive engineering, manufacturing, material science or related fields. Admission is based on academic achievement and program specific requirements.

sections.title: 2. How long is PG in mechanical engineering in France?

items: In **France**, a **national Master’s degree** normally takes **two years** of study following a relevant bachelor’s degree. Some programs may allow suitably qualified candidates to enter directly into the second year.

sections.title: 3. Can I do PG mechanical engineering in France in English?

items: "Yes. Some French universities and engineering schools offer **master’s programs in mechanical engineering and related technical disciplines taught in English** Students are advised to check the language of instruction of the program of their choice.

sections.title: 4. What is the cost of mechanical engineering PG in France?

items: For **2026-2027**The public-university Master's reference fee is €255 per year for eligible French and EU students and €3,950 per year for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. International specialized programs and private institutions may charge different fees.

sections.title: 5. What are the jobs after mechanical engineering PG in France?

items: Depending on their specialization and experience, graduates can work as **mechanical design engineers**, **automotive engineers**, **aerospace engineers**, **manufacturing engineers**, **robotics engineers**, **mechatronics engineers** and **research and development engineers**.

Students are advised to check the qualification awarded and its recognition prior to enrollment.
* A national Master’s degree is part of the French and European higher education system.
Before applying, students should verify the following:
- The exact title of your degree and the awarding institution.
- The qualification is a national Master’s degree or an engineering diploma.
- Duration of the program and ECTS credits.
- Current accreditation status as applicable.
- Internship, lab and research opportunities.
- Eligibility for doctoral study or advanced professional education.
Students should not assume that all programs called a master’s or engineering course give the same qualification or recognition.

Graduates of ****postgraduate courses in mechanical engineering in France**** can go on to work in the manufacturing industry, automotive technology, aerospace, robotics, energy, industrial automation and research.
**Possible mechanical engineering job titles:**
- Design engineer (mechanical).
- Project Engineer Mechanical
- Engineer, automotive.
- Aerospace engineering
- Engineer, Manufacturing.
- Engineer in production.
- Robotics engineer.
- Mechatronics engineer.
- Materials engineering.
-Thermal systems engineer
- Quality engineer.
- Research & Development Engineer.
Your chances of getting a job will depend on your technical skills, work experience, language skills and work permit, as well as the specialization you choose.

****Salaries for mechanical engineers in France**** are affected by the employer, location, qualifications, industry and professional experience. Have students examine current job advertisements and salary surveys for particular engineering positions to determine possible pay.
Typical ****Documents for Mechanical Engineering PG Applications in France**** are:
- Passport valid for 6 months.
- Bachelor’s degree certificate or provisional degree certificate.
- Academic transcripts (official).
- CV (Curriculum vitae).
- SOP (Statement of Purpose) or motivation letter.
- test results in English or French, if necessary.
- Recommendation letters (if required).
- Certificates of internship/work experience (if any).
- Technical portfolio or research proposal as appropriate.
- Document translation when certified translation is necessary.
- Application form and proof of payment, if applicable.
- Financial and visa documentation at the appropriate stage.
The exact list of documents is institution and program-specific. Applicants should review the official admissions checklist and see if certified copies or specific translation formats are required.
